pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher's Welcome - The Archbishop's School Canterbury
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
The Archbishop's School welcomes you to our vibrant, caring, and supportive Christian Community.
The Archbishop's School is a mixed ability school for students aged 11-19.
The school community is smaller than most secondary schools, enabling us to provide a personalised approach to education.
All students are well known, well cared for and receive the very best support and encouragement in their learning which engenders excellent progress in their academic, personal, social and spiritual development. Our school ethos is “Enter to Learn - Go Forth to Serve”. This perfectly describes our mission: to provide the very best education for our students, whilst preparing them for school life in the twenty-first century with all the challenges this presents. They are able to make a positive contribution to society and share the love of God.
As an innovative and forward-thinking school, we celebrate all of our students' achievements and are extremely proud of the people they become.
Welcome to The Archbishop's School.
Mr D. Elliott, Headteacher

Holly A, one of our Year 12 students played a role in the campaign to keep the Thanington Recreation Ground open, and subsequently received a Community Spirit award. Holly said: “The council were trying to turn Thanington Recreation Ground into a multi-story car park, and I gave a speech which helped to keep it open.” Scroll across to read our interview with Holly. We are incredibly proud of Holly. By speaking with confidence, compassion and courage, Holly showed how young people can make a real difference in their community. Well done Holly.
HeadteacherMr D Elliott

pageCache.pageTitle: A-Level Results 2026 - News - The Archbishop's School Canterbury
pageCache.text:
News
A-Level Results 2026
The Archbishop’s School would like to congratulate our Sixth Form students on today’s examination results. We have been immensely proud of their leadership and contribution to our school community throughout their time at The Archbishop’s School and we are delighted to celebrate their success. Special mention goes to our three highest achieving students who gained A*A*A, Dist*Dist*Dist, and A*AB respectively.
38% of our students obtained an A or A* or equivalent in at least one of their subjects. There were A or A* or equivalent grades in Art & Design, Arabic, Biology, Business, Chemistry, Criminology, Law, Mathematics, Sociology, and Sport. We have students going on to study a wide range of subjects at university including medicine, chemistry, sports journalism, law, business management, and physiotherapy. Whether going to university, taking up an apprenticeship, going out into the world of work, or enjoying a gap year, we know that they will continue to make the school proud by serving their communities, sharing their talents and showing what exceptional people they have become. Mr. Elliott, Headteacher, said "our students continue to amaze and inspire me with their hard work and dedication, leading to some truly brilliant outcomes, we could not be prouder of them all".
HeadteacherMr D Elliott

pageCache.pageTitle: GCSE Results 2026 - News - The Archbishop's School Canterbury
pageCache.text:
News
GCSE Results 2026
The Archbishop’s School has once again seen results improve at GCSE level to celebrate what are now the best results since at least 2018! We continued to achieve close to 10% of results at grades 7-9 and achieved grade 9s in nine different subjects including Spanish, Mathematics, Religious Studies, Science, and students’ Heritage Languages. Equally, once again, well over 50% of students achieved grade 4 or better in English and Mathematics and five or more grades at 4+. A third of grades were at grade 5 or better, with 26 students achieving grade 5 or better in all their subjects. It was a lovely experience to watch so many happy and excited students celebrating with their friends, family, and staff at the school yesterday. Mr Elliott, Headteacher, said:
“We are delighted for our student body who have performed brilliantly. The average grade is up again – a great reflection of the hard work of our students and staff.”
We look forward to seeing many of you back as part of our growing and ever-more successful Sixth Form. To all those moving onto Grammar Schools or College, we wish you all the best and know that you are welcome back at the school at any point in the future. Well done to you all.
HeadteacherMr D Elliott

Parental Communication Systems
My Child at School (MCAS) Application
The MCAS application offers a convenient and efficient way for you to stay engaged with your child's education. You will be able to access various features in the app including attendance, class information, co-curricular (clubs and interventions), examination data, options information, parental consent, reports, and student timetables.
Once you have installed the MCAS app, we encourage all parents and carers to ensure that you check your MCAS account regularly to stay up to date with announcements from the school.
Link: MyChildAtSchool - Login
Please read the guide here to learn how to log into the MCAS portal: How-To-Log-Into-MCAS-portal.pdf
We have produced a useful FAQ document here: MCAS-FAQ-10.10.2025.pdf
ClassCharts
Link: https://www.classcharts.com/parent/login
ClassCharts is a behavioural monitoring system which also features a rewards shop/resource for students who reach certain positive point milestones and can choose a reward.
We encourage all parents/carers (and students) to download the application and obtain a login for ClassCharts to support us with your child’s behaviour, both positive and negative.

pageCache.text:
Careers at The Archbishop’s School - In Association With
Unifrog
All students who attend The Archbishop’s School in Years 7 – Sixth Form have access to Unifrog. Unifrog is an award winning, online careers platform that allows students the ability to search an extensive online careers library to support the delivery of our School Careers Programme.
Focusing on self-awareness, self-determination and self-exploration of skills and interests for our Key Stage 3 students with accelerated use within Key Stage 4 and Sixth Form, focusing on Labour Market Information, exploring career pathways, Post 14, 16 and 18 choices and preparing for the world of work.
The Archbishop’s School are also pleased to offer a parental login to parents if they so wish to explore this platform with their child.
Please contact the Careers Team if you would like to be set up with a parental login.
TEP
The Archbishop’s School is proud to be working with The Education People. The Education People Skills & Employability service is committed to supporting, promoting and delivering high quality services for secondary school aged children on behalf of Kent County Council. Conducted in order to raise aspirations and equip young people with the skills they need to reach their full potential in adult life.
The Education People hold the strategic and operational responsibilities in Kent for the ‘Raising the Participation Age’ (RPA) duties placed on local authorities by the government.
Careers and Enterprise Company
The Archbishop’s School works closely with The Careers and Enterprise Company (The CEC). We are pleased to be able to work collaboratively within school with our Enterprise Co-ordinator (Vickie Pennell) who works with us in delivering against our Gatsby Benchmarks and completing our Compass+ evaluations.
The school commits to evaluating the careers programme by completing the Compass+ evaluations in Autumn and Spring with a final evaluation that includes all completed activities for the year, being the most accurate evaluation of the careers programme. Regular feedback is provided to SLT and our Link Governor.

SEND
Introduction
As a school we always seek to find the most appropriate intervention or support for our students.
We are committed to providing the very best support for our most vulnerable students.
We seek to create an enriching and supportive environment in which all students can flourish and fulfil their potential academically, spiritually, physically, and socially.
We screen all Year 7 students using a variety of methods including specialist assessments, which underpin our identification of SEND processes.
These also support teaching staff in ensuring that we provide quality-first inclusive teaching.
Our core offer incorporates high quality evidence-based intervention programmes that cover all areas as set out in the Code of Practice.
The Archbishop's School has one Specialist Resourced Provision to support students with specific learning difficulties which is led by a specialist teacher. Lessons are tied into the humanities curriculum models and incorporate independent learning skills, assistive technologies as well as a small group setting to support the development of specific learning difficulty skills.
Learning Support
Our school’s core Christian values and ethos define all that we do for the support of our students with special educational needs and disabilities.
Our shared purpose is to develop a positive and supportive learning environment where all young people can excel and take all that they have learnt, socially and morally in to the wider community as they develop as young adults.
Our Key Aims
Ensure a person centered approach to learning.
Our Specialist Resourced Provision
Specific Learning Difficulty (SpLD) - In-Class Support, Bespoke Literacy Interventions, Assistive Technology.
